Dev’s pattern across the sessions is consistent: he keeps apologizing and missing, and every excuse is the same one. He’s “head down in the archive” (t0, t2, t6), keeps saying he “genuinely want[s] to come” but can’t, and repeatedly defers real attendance to “when the PhD is done” (t2, t6, t8). He misses the Amsterdam/October planning, then November, then “the Saturday,” then the June 30 session — and Kwame confirms he’s been “MIA for like six weeks” (t6). So what was pulling him away is clear: his PhD/archival research. He wasn’t disengaging deliberately; he was being pulled out by the archive work, constantly promising to return once the PhD was finished.

The conversation first signals the shift at the very start, in Dev’s first message (t0, June 2): he opens with “sorry, head down in the archive all morning” and hedges on October (“October is tricky but I don’t want to say no yet”). That is the earliest sign that the archive is already pulling him away, and every later message is just a repeat of the same pattern.

By Session 3, after Abi cancelled for the third time, his position shifted entirely: 'I'm not going to plan another ambitious trip. Let's do something local and actually doable.' He moved from enthusiasm for group trips to insisting on small, confirmed, local events — and from waiting for consensus to proposing specific dates with booking commitments.
